clue.text: Teaching assistant in school going back to mark

indicators.note: the assistant is placed in the school, so these letters go inside the other piece
the school's name is read backwards, as if returning

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A classroom helper at a school heads back to do some marking.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English public school; 'mark' is the verb, to write down.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to write something down in symbols, a way of setting a mark on paper.

clue.text: Bit out of end of pen ran

parts.note: the nib is the writing tip at the end of a pen
colours that run are said to bleed, so ran gives bled

explanation.surface: Some ink seeped out of the tip of a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' is the past tense of bite, not a small piece; 'out of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nibbled is past tense of taking small bites, so it matches 'bit' as a verb.

clue.text: Prepare to drive Peugeot: go out for a spin

indicators.note: letters taken for a spin are whirled round into a new order
go out tells us the letters of go are removed from the car's name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone readies a Peugeot to take it out for a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing G and O ('out') leaves PEUET, which 'for a spin' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, you tee up the ball before striking a drive off the tee.

clue.text: Food in bags to carry out

indicators.note: the bagging word carries the other inside it, so it holds those letters

parts.note: to bag something is to take it, so bags gives takes
someone out is away

explanation.surface: Meals packed in bags for customers to carry out of the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The whole clue reads like a plain definition, which hides that 'bags' and 'out' are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals bought ready-made from a shop or restaurant to eat elsewhere are called takeaways in Britain.

clue.text: Tear page off a tiny bit to see item in paper

indicators.note: tearing at a word rips part of it away, signalling a removal
off says the page's letter is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: a particle is a tiny bit of something

explanation.surface: Someone rips a scrap from a page to look at a piece in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear ... off' strips P from PARTICLE; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is made up of pieces of writing, each called an article.

clue.text: Bankers from Santander moving slowly

indicators.note: the remaining letters are moved around into a new order
the banks of a word are its outer letters, so bankers removed from it leaves the inside

explanation.surface: Staff at Santander bank are slow to get anything done.
explanation.walkthrough: Santander is a bank, but 'Bankers from' strips the outer S and R; 'moving' rearranges ANTANDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Walker's my name

definitions.meaning: a vagrant who walks the roads, or a long hike
The pseudonym of the setter of this crossword

explanation.surface: A rambler introduces themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant travels on foot, and the setter signs this puzzle with that pseudonym.

clue.text: Picking up nose on wine after you and taster ultimately agreed

indicators.note: the wine comes after the other pieces in the answer
picking up a sound means hearing it, so we want a word said like slang for nose

parts.note: conk is British slang for the nose

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letters of the words you and taster

parts.note: red is wine of that colour

explanation.surface: A wine taster sniffing a glass of red agrees with your verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picking up' turns CONK into its sound-alike CONC; 'ultimately' takes the last letters U and R; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to share the same opinion, which is what agreeing means.

clue.text: Opening line on film: watch at the start

indicators.note: the watching word goes at the start of the answer
in a down answer, L sits on top of the film

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
ET is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: The first line of a film's script tells you to keep watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' is the noun, a small hole, not the start of a film.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small hole, usually reinforced, through which a lace or cord passes.

clue.text: Shot fired over man's head with the other hand

indicators.note: in this down clue the changed word stretches over the extra letter, holding it
swapping hands turns right into left, so the letter for right becomes the letter for left
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gun goes off above someone's head while held in the left hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the other hand' changes R (right) in FIRED to L (left), making FILED; 'over' wraps it round M from 'head' of man's.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting a scene with a camera is filming it, so shot works as filmed.

clue.text: Trump to take five women home before date

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the date in the answer

parts.note: to take five is to have a short break
in means at home

explanation.surface: A politician named Trump pauses to bring five women home before a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' is British slang for passing wind, not the politician; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to trump is to fart, which is the meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: Nurses stripped for show

indicators.note: stripping a word removes its outer layers, its first and last letters

parts.note: nannies are children's nurses

explanation.surface: Nurses take their clothes off for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' removes N and S from NANNIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is a well-known Broadway musical about an orphan girl.

clue.text: Smashing plate for bread in old Greece

indicators.note: smashing breaks the word into pieces to be put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: At a Greek meal, plates are smashed with bread on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepta were small coins of ancient Greece, and bread is slang for money.

clue.text: Change for writer with no break

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themselves as me
a pause is a short break

explanation.surface: A novelist works on without any interruption to transform things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' is the euphemism 'the change of life'; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The time a woman stops menstruating is often called the change, short for change of life.

clue.text: Dealt with small vehicle parts for scrap

indicators.note: the outer word parts, splitting open to hold the other letters

parts.note: if you dealt with a task you did it
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone sorted out a small car, breaking it for parts for the scrapyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' splits DID to hold SCAR; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap something is to throw it away as unwanted, the same as to discard it.

clue.text: Pen to run out describing husband? Turn over

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: liquid that runs out slowly seeps
to fold something is to turn part of it over

explanation.surface: A writer's pen leaks while he writes about a husband, so he turns the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' is an enclosure, not a writing tool; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepfold is an enclosure for keeping sheep, a kind of animal pen.

clue.text: Space in front of bay to take ship

indicators.note: the space comes in front of the next piece in the answer

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
a dog's bay is its bark

explanation.surface: Room in front of a bay where a ship can be boarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' is the noise a dog makes, not the coastal inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go aboard a vessel, which is what taking ship means.

clue.text: Stands in front of royals: guards, at the start, going for their headgear

indicators.note: the first piece comes in front of the other in the answer

parts.note: to bear is to stand or tolerate something

indicators.note: the letter taken from guards goes, being removed

parts.note: kings are royals

indicators.note: picks the first letter of the word guards

explanation.surface: Guards stand before the royal family wearing their tall hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' takes G from guards, and 'going' removes it from KINGS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal guards at Buckingham Palace wear tall fur hats called bearskins.

clue.text: Debate about a boy

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An argument over a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason with someone is to argue logically, as in a debate.

clue.text: Signs section for work

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Signposts for a section of road works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices are posted signs carrying information or warnings.

clue.text: One brought back to earth after Sun's character assassination

indicators.note: the craft comes after the Sun letter

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun, with 's as is
a lander is a craft that brings people back down to land

explanation.surface: A tabloid called the Sun smears someone and brings them down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, but here it just gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Character assassination is damaging someone's reputation with false spoken claims.

clue.text: Enigmatic person is cross after panic outside hospital

indicators.note: the cross comes after the other piece
the panic word sits outside the hospital letter

parts.note: to be in a spin is to panic
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure gets angry after a panic outside a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; 'cross' is the letter X, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphinx is a person whose thoughts are inscrutable, after the riddling Sphinx of myth.

clue.text: Disease obtained from insects? Not primarily

indicators.note: without the primary, or first, letter

parts.note: crickets are chirping insects

explanation.surface: Asking whether an illness can be caught from bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtained from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickets is a childhood bone disease caused by lack of vitamin D.

clue.text: Does hot food, following starter of chicken

indicators.note: the other pieces follow the chicken letter
the starter is the first letter of the word chicken

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: A cook makes some hot food after a chicken starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' means swindles, as in 'did him out of money', not performs.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for swindling them, which is what someone who cheats does.

clue.text: Teacher's perhaps after hard work and playground activity

indicators.note: the whisky comes after the other pieces

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
op, short for opus, is a work
Teacher's is a brand of Scotch whisky; perhaps marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A teacher's playground duty after a hard day's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's' is the whisky brand, not a schoolteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's game hopping between chalked squares, often played at school break.

clue.text: Stop runs from part of wicket

indicators.note: runs taken from the word means its letter is removed

parts.note: the crease is a line marked on a cricket pitch at the wicket
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket match halts as runs come from the wicket area.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is a line by the wicket in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to come to an end, the same as to stop.

clue.text: So nurses against patient

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus
to can mean against, as in face to face

explanation.surface: So nurses oppose a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' is a verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures hardship without complaint, showing great patience.

clue.text: Like one that gets laid? Love endless sex squeezing butt

indicators.note: the outer letters squeeze the cask inside them

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: endless removes both ends of the word

parts.note: a butt is a large cask, like a vat

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about love, sex and someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips S and X from sex; one 'that gets laid' is an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovate means egg-shaped, and an egg is what gets laid by a hen.

clue.text: Middle of day, run out to get mum bouquet

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word day

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
ma is mother, mum

explanation.surface: At midday someone dashes out to buy flowers for their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' is a wine's smell, not flowers; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its characteristic smell.

clue.text: One running around with single escort

parts.note: c, for circa, means around
and means with
I is one, single
to date is to escort someone

explanation.surface: A jogger out with an unmarried companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' means standing for election.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone running for office is a candidate standing in the election.

clue.text: Blues band replacing member with Suggs at the front

indicators.note: one letter is replaced by another

parts.note: Madness is a British ska-pop band
M is the member at the front of the band's name, Suggs's place

indicators.note: the first letter of Suggs

explanation.surface: A band swaps a member for Suggs as frontman.
explanation.walkthrough: Suggs is the lead singer of Madness, a British ska band; its first letter replaces M.
explanation.definitionFit: The blues is a state of low spirits, so it means sorrow.

clue.text: Advantages of good grades put before classes

indicators.note: the grades are put before the classes

parts.note: A's are the top grades
sets are school classes grouped by ability

explanation.surface: Top marks count for more than which class you're in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are useful qualities or resources, things that give one an advantage.
